topics.transcript: Palpitations in primary care: when to worry. Key points. Palpitations are a common presentation. First, take a history—regular or irregular, duration, triggers. Consider anxiety and mental health overlap; many patients have both cardiac concerns and anxiety. If red flags—syncope, chest pain, shortness of breath—arrange ECG and consider referral. Holter monitoring may be needed for intermittent symptoms. NICE guidance recommends assessing for underlying arrhythmia and checking thyroid function. Always document and follow up.

topics.title: The overlap between COPD and heart disease
topics.filename: Ep 42 – The overlap between COPD and heart disease.mp3
topics.transcript: The overlap between COPD and heart disease. Patients with COPD often have cardiovascular comorbidity. Breathlessness may be pulmonary, cardiac, or both. Assess for heart failure, ischaemic heart disease, and atrial fibrillation. Use QRISK and consider statins; manage blood pressure. Spirometry helps confirm COPD; BNP or NT-proBNP can help distinguish cardiac cause. Integrated care and medication review are key. NICE and BTS guidance support combined assessment.
